passage:
Every Wednesday morning, two students read school news on the radio. They talk about tests, club activities, lost items, and lunch menus.
At first, most students did not listen carefully. The voices sounded nervous, and the news was not exciting.
Then the radio team added a new part called "One Good Thing." Students could write down something kind they saw at school. The team read one story each week.
Soon, students listened more closely. They heard about a boy who helped clean spilled soup, a teacher who stayed late for a student, and a class that shared umbrellas during heavy rain.
The school radio did not become louder. It became more meaningful.
